'''''Armeria maritima''''', the '''thrift''', '''sea thrift''' or '''sea pink''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Plumbaginaceae]]. It is a compact [[evergreen]] [[Perennial plant|perennial]] which grows in low clumps and sends up long stems that support globes of bright pink flowers. In some cases purple, white or red flowers also occur. It is a popular garden flower and has been distributed worldwide as a garden and cut flower.  It does well in gardens designed as [[xeriscaping|xeriscapes]] or [[rock garden]]s. The Latin specific epithet ''maritima'' means pertaining to the sea or coastal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Armeria maritima - Plant Finder|url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285144|access-date=2021-12-21|website=[[Missouri Botanical Garden]]}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
[[File:Pescadero Beach - panoramio.jpg|thumb|''Armeria maritima californica'' at [[Pescadero State Beach]] in California|left]]
[[File:Sea Pinks.png|thumb|left|Sea Pinks in Cornwall]]
''Armeria maritima'' [[Glossary of botanical terms#sensu lato|sensu lato]] has a circumpolar distribution and can be found in the wild in coastal areas across the Northern Hemisphere.<ref name= powo/><ref name="Stace"/> It can grow in dry, sandy, saline conditions such as coastal cliffs, [[grassland]] and [[salt marsh]]es, salted roadsides and inland on mountain rocks.<ref name="Stace">{{cite book|last=Stace|first=C. A.|author-link = Stace, C. A.|year=2019|title=New Flora of the British Isles|publisher=C & M Floristics |isbn=978-1-5272-2630-2 |edition=Fourth |location=Middlewood Green, Suffolk, U.K.}}</ref>{{rp|461}}<ref name=Blamey>{{cite book|last1=Blamey|first1=M.|last2=Fitter|first2=R.|last3=Fitter|first3=A|year=2003|title=Wild flowers of Britain and Ireland: The Complete Guide to the British and Irish Flora.|publisher=A & C Black|location=London|isbn=978-1408179505}}</ref>{{rp|70}} It is common in [[Great Britain|British]] salt marshes, where it flowers April to October.<ref>[https://www.wildlifetrusts.org/wildlife-explorer/wildflowers/thrift Wildlife Trusts - Thrift]</ref>

''Armeria maritima'' has a great [[copper]]-tolerance, and is able to grow in [[soil]]s with copper concentrations of up to 6400 mg/kg.  One mechanism proposed is that not much copper is transported up the shoot of the plant, and is excreted from decaying leaves.<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Brewin LE, Mehra A, Lynch PT, Farago ME |title=Mechanisms of copper tolerance by ''Armeria maritima'' in Dolfrwyong Bog, north Wales—initial studies |journal=Environ Geochem Health |volume=25 |issue=1 |pages=147–56 |date=March 2003 |doi=10.1023/a:1021225721605 |pmid=12901090 |s2cid=36813793 |url=http://www.kluweronline.com/art.pdf?issn=0269-4042&volume=25&page=147}}</ref> Some of the physiology and metabolism of this species has been described, of particular note is how the metabolism of this species is altered with elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide concentrations.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Davey | first1 = M. P. | last2 = Harmens | first2 = H. | last3 = Ashenden | first3 = T. W. | last4 = Edwards | first4 = R. | last5 = Baxter | first5 = R. | title = Species-specific effects of elevated CO<sub>2</sub> on resource allocation in ''Plantago maritima'' and ''Armeria maritima'' | doi = 10.1016/j.bse.2006.09.004 | journal = Biochemical Systematics and Ecology | volume = 35 | issue = 3 | page = 121 | year = 2007 | bibcode = 2007BioSE..35..121D }}</ref>

==Ecology==
[[File:20230519 Gewöhnliche Grasnelke (Armeria maritima).jpg|thumb|left|Armeria maritima with bee ([[Hiddensee]] Island)]]
[[File:Sea thrift on the Pembrokeshire coast path.jpg|thumb|left|Sea thrift on the Pembrokeshire coast path]]
Pollination is by various insects including [[bees]] and [[Lepidoptera]].

It is a known host species to the [[pathogenic]] fungus ''[[Phoma herbarum]]''.<ref Name="HH&GGE2004">Helgi Hallgrímsson & Guðríður Gyða Eyjólfsdóttir (2004). [https://rafhladan.is/bitstream/handle/10802/4090/Fjolrit_45.pdf?sequence=1 ''Íslenskt sveppatal I - smásveppir'' [Checklist of Icelandic Fungi I - Microfungi]. Fjölrit Náttúrufræðistofnunar. Náttúrufræðistofnun Íslands [Icelandic Institute of Natural History]. ISSN 1027-832X</ref>

==Conservation==
''Armeria maritima'' is a common species in the UK, however there are several subspecies and in England, subspecies ''elongata'' (Tall Thrift) has vulnerable conservation status and is designated as a [[List of species and habitats of principal importance in England|species of principal importance]] for biodiversity conservation under the [[Natural Environment and Rural Communities Act 2006|NERC Act (2006)]].

==Cultivation==
The [[cultivar]] 'Vindictive' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/96568/Armeria-maritima-Vindictive/Details | title = ''Armeria maritima'' 'Vindictive' | website = www.rhs.org | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 12 April 2020}}</ref> 

==In popular culture==
[[Image:Threepence 1943.jpg|thumb|A 1943 [[threepence (British coin)]]]]
The [[Threepence (British coin)|British threepence coin]] issued between 1937 and 1952 had a design of thrift on the reverse. The word thrift also means the practice of frugality, being careful with money and so avoiding waste. So, in light of the economic depression of the 1930s and the privations of the Second World War the choice of the thrift plant for the design of the new 12-sided nickel-brass threepenny bit (3d coin) which was replacing the silver three old pence coin (with origins going back to the mid-sixteenth century) was apt. With the accession of Queen Elizabeth II in 1952, the thrift plant with its three flower heads was replaced on threepenny bit with a crowned portcullis, recalling a royal badge used by Queen Elizabeth I and her predecessors from the House of Tudor.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/thrift |title=thrift noun - Definition, pictures, pronunciation and usage notes | Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary at |publisher=Oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com |date= |accessdate=2022-05-06}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://theresagreen.me/tag/thrift-on-old-three-pence-coin/|title = Thrift on old three pence coin}}</ref>

As part of a 2002 marketing campaign, the plant conservation charity Plantlife chose sea thrift as the [[County flowers of the United Kingdom|county flower]] of the [[Isles of Scilly]].
